newsitem.title: USA: Benzidine makers sued for NJ bladder cancers.
newsitem.headline: Benzidine makers sued for NJ bladder cancers.

text.p: The law firm of Wilentz, Goldman & Spitzer PA said it has filed a third complaint in New Jersey Superior Court, Middlesex County, seeking damages from suppliers of benzidine-containing products to Allied Textile Printers, a Paterson, N.J., company that went out of business in 1982.
The firm said the latest suit was filed in the New Brunswick, N.J., court on behalf of George Roignant alleging that his bladder cancer was caused by the use of benzidine-containing products.
Benzidine, a carcinogen, was found in color dyes and pigment powders used to dye fabrics during his employment with Allied Textile from 1957 to 1982, the firm's statement said.
Medical literature has demonstrated a causal link between benzidine exposure and bladder cancer, it explained.
For years prior to the closing of the Allied plant in 1982, employees regularly handled benzidine-containing products without any protective equipment, it said.

The defendants named in this lawsuit thus far are the suppliers of benzidine-containing products to the Allied plant including American Cyanamid Corp, now a unit of American Home Products Corp ; Ciba Speciality Holding Inc ; Clairant Corp, formerly Sandoz Chemical Corp; DuPont Co ; GAF Corp, Novartis AG, formerly Ciba-Geigy and Raclaur Inc.
All of these defendants supplied benzidine-containing products without proper warnings and Roignant was exposed to these products, the statement said.

Early last month and in December 1996, Wilentz, Goldman & Spitzer said, it filed two wrongful death complaints on behalf of widows whose husbands worked at the Allied plant. Both men passed away due to bladder cancer. The same defendants were included in the two wrongful death complaints.
The firm said the complaint's counts include negligence, breach of warranty, strict liability, absolute liability, misrepresentation, products liability and loss of consortium.

Assisting the Wilentz firm in this matter are the Ness, Motley firm of South Carolina, the Youngdahl, Sadin & Morgan firm in New Mexico and the law offices of Thomas J. Lamb in North Carolina. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212 859-1610))
